newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher for third session.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher for third session.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Thursday for the third consecutive day with yields on long CPI-linked bonds falling to a two-year low, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.02 pct to 103.51
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct at 102.75
Volume was high at 188 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in the Makams.

"The positive momentum in the bond market continued with yields on CPI-linked long bonds falling to only 4.1-4.15 percent, their lowest level in the last 24 months," said a trader at IBI Investment House.
"Inflation-linked bonds made a very big move this week rising by more than one percent. Today the rise was very moderate," said Yossi Weidelfeld of Eyal Securities.
Both traders said CPI-linked bonds had strengthened this week on the back of expectations for higher inflation but, they added, prices would probably stabilise next week.
In spite of the inflationary expectations, unlinked bonds also continued to rise today, traders said.
"With yields on inflation-linked short bonds falling to only 3.8-3.9 percent a yield of 14.4 percent on unlinked bonds is becoming more attractive," the IBI trader said.
"The rise in unlinked bonds index does not reflect the whole rise because today was the expiry date of one of the Gilon series," which he said moderated the index's rise.
Weidelfeld said unlinked bonds and Makams were catching up with the rise in linked bonds and trading in them was relatively heavy.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds continued rising in response to another decline of the shekel against the dollar in the local forex market today. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3700 shekels against 3.3670 shekels on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
